subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What should the canonical inbound-media isolation boundary be across agents and channels: account-scoped, agent/session-scoped, tenant-aware, explicit-share based, or a staged combination?
rationale: The issue is security-sensitive, and a narrow account-subdir patch would set durable storage, reference, staging, and sharing semantics without clear maintainer intent.

options.title: Define the scoped media contract first
options.body: Choose the ownership model, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

options.title: Ship account scoping as an interim boundary
options.body: Implement the lower-friction account-based directory model while explicitly accepting follow-up work for non-1:1 account-to-agent and tenant-sharing cases.

options.title: Defer broad core change
options.body: Leave only narrower channel-specific issues active until a maintainer sponsors the cross-channel core media-isolation design.

recommendation.title: Define the scoped media contract first
recommendation.body: Choose the ownership model, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He has current and recent history on the central media/staging files and already reviewed this issue as the broad tracker.
